query: FCC high-entropy alloys lose substantial strength above 800 °C, motivating refractory high-entropy alloys. Equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW retains excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but has poor room-temperature ductility, and its irradiation resistance has been inferred computationally rather than established here experimentally. Studies of other refractory high-entropy alloys have found greater irradiation resistance than pure tungsten under helium implantation and self-healing behavior associated with enhanced atomic diffusion and redistribution. However, irradiation-induced amorphization, helium-energy-dependent blistering, and irradiation-enhanced precipitation have also been observed, indicating unresolved phase- and surface-stability risks. Given the need to preserve BCC structural stability and high-temperature mechanical performance while improving room-temperature ductility and irradiation tolerance, what intervention could achieve this balance? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted directional or quantitative outcomes relative to untreated NbMoTaW, the applicable temperature and irradiation boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a group IV element, such as Ti, to the refractory high-entropy alloy NbMoTaW will improve its room-temperature ductility while preserving its high-temperature mechanical performance and BCC structural stability.
generation.intervention: Addition of a group IV element, such as Ti
generation.conditions: Room temperature and high-temperature (up to 1600 °C) conditions
generation.structural_mediator: Dislocation core asymmetry and vibrational properties
generation.mechanism: The addition of a group IV element will induce core asymmetry in the dislocation structure, leading to enhanced dislocation mobility and improved ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature ductility and preserved high-temperature mechanical performance
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to 1600 °C; irradiation conditions: helium implantation
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of group IV element to be added and the potential effects on irradiation tolerance are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of NbMoTaW with varying amounts of added group IV element (e.g., Ti) at room temperature and high temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of a group IV element does not improve room-temperature ductility or compromises high-temperature mechanical performance, the hypothesis is falsified.
